payload.title: [server-storage-3] Cross-app presence eviction: presence_leases ON CONFLICT lets app B overwrite/evict app A's l...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING server-storage-3 (low/isolation, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/storage/presence-store.ts
LINES: 40-52

WHAT: presence_leases PRIMARY KEY is (tenant_id, presence_type, presence_key) with app_id additive (migrations.ts 0003/0021). set() does `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(tenant_id, presence_type, presence_key) DO UPDATE SET app_id = excluded.app_id, packed = excluded.packed, expires_at = excluded.expires_at`. read()/clear() filter by app_id. So when App B sets a lease at a (tenant,type,key) already held by App A, B's write overwrites the row and rewrites app_id to B. App A's subsequent read() (filtered app_id=A) then returns undefined — A's presence was silently evicted by B, and B observes its own value. There is no cross-app guard (unlike ObjectStore/BlobStore).

IMPACT: In a multi-app deployment two apps sharing a (tenant, presence_type, presence_key) tuple can evict each other's presence leases. Bounded blast radius (presence is ephemeral/TTL'd and apps usually use distinct keys/schemas); single-app deployments unaffected.

SUGGESTED FIX: Include app_id in the presence_leases primary key (additive migration in both dialect files) and target ON CONFLICT on the app-scoped key, or add a FrickCrossAppAccessError-style guard before the upsert.
